title: Grateful Dead Live at Oklahoma City Fairgrounds Arena on 1973-10-19

ai_review.summary: Vault‑remastered soundboard captures a solid 1973 show highlighted by a smoking Dark Star/MLB jam and crisp Jerry work, despite some early mix quirks.
ai_review.review: The performance shines on the second set – Dark Star into the first Mind Left Body (MLB) jam, Morning Dew, Playing In The Band and an inspired Eyes of the World/​Stella Blue encore are repeatedly praised.  Jerry’s tone is described as crisp and dexterous, Phil delivers a standout solo and bomb‑filled low end, while the mix, though a bit unbalanced at the start of the first set, settles into a clear, well‑separated soundboard recording that most listeners find very listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating across 15 substantive reviews is ~4.3; the majority of comments are positive about both performance and sound quality, with only a few isolated criticisms.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Vault‑remastered SBD; early first‑set balance favors keyboards over guitars, but levels correct quickly.  Mix is clear with Jerry and Weir well separated left/right; occasional minor sloppiness noted but overall crisp and listenable.

poor_songs: China > Rider (feeling groovy deemed weak by some)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set starts uneven with balance and energy issues, picks up after 'Don't Ease Me In' and builds to a strong Playing In The Band.  Second set is high‑energy, featuring extended jams and the first solid MLB jam, culminating in an enthusiastic encore.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as crisp, dexterous and on fire during Dark Star, MLB jam and solos throughout; great tone and vocal presence on Sugaree.
band_member_comments.Phil: Delivers a “phil‑tastic” solo in Dark Star and powerful bass bombs in Morning Dew, adding depth to the improvisations.
band_member_comments.Keys: Early mix lets keyboards dominate before balance is corrected; Keith syncs tightly with guitars during jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming noted as energetic (extra limbs), driving the high‑octane moments in Playing In The Band and second‑set jams.
